simple.meaning: כֻּסֶּמֶת (kuççemeth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “spelt (from its bristliness as if just shorn ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 9:32. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כֻּסֶּמֶת (H3698) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: כֻּסֶּמֶת (kuççemeth) / H3698 is traced through Exodus 9:32, Isaiah 28:25, Ezekiel 4:9 with generated occurrence evidence.

structuredEvidence.definition: spelt (from its bristliness as if just shorn )

firstOccurrence.englishText: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they had not grown up.

timeline.evidenceText: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they had not grown up.
When he has leveled its surface, doesn’t he plant the dill, and scatter the cumin seed, and put in the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place?

“Take for yourself also wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and put them in one vessel. Make bread of it. According to the number of the days that you will lie on your side, even three hundred ninety days, you shall eat of it.
